children: , the social-media and consumer-AI company, unveiled plans to bring Muse to its AI glasses and previewed Charm, a pocket-sized device for talking to the agent. Shares dropped by 2.8% to $755.815 at 10.13 am ET time on September 25, 2026. The ambition is clear: give people more reasons to reach for Meta's AI throughout the dayand more devices through which to use it.

According to Meta, Muse will respond to what users see through their glasses, handle tasks while conversations continue and get its own email address. Shopping, payments and work integrations widen its potential uses, while Meta plans more than 100 AI-glasses styles by year-end. The revenue expectations are already substantial. Reuters reported that Jefferies estimated $10.8 billion in annualized revenue if Muse reaches 1 billion users by the end of 2027 and at least 3% become paying customers. That is a scenario, not money in the bank.

The September 25 valuation snapshot puts Meta 11.73% below its $856.24 GF Value estimate, suggesting potential upside without proving the shares are a bargain. The real test is repeat use that pays. Subscriptions, purchases and advertising could turn Muse into another earnings engine, but each needs to generate revenue without driving users away. More glasses can expand distribution. Retention, device margins and revenue per user will show whether that reach translates into profit.

title: Meta Drops 2.8% as Muse Escapes the Smartphone
